title: Steel Tide Week 1 Update
author: Reasonable-Reason901
selftext:
This is the progress on my Mech/RTS game after the first week. I added co-op a few days ago and have been playing it with my wife and a friend. Still working through tons of issues and trying to balance feature work with stability but it's been an absolute joy seeing it come to life and having complete creative freedom to just dream up your ideal game and then go make it real. Feedback is welcome! 

  


# Co-op

* Play with up to 3 people: two mech pilots and one commander
* Empty seats get filled by AI, so you can play solo too
* Battles with over 50,000 units on the field at once
* If someone disconnects, they can reconnect and jump back into the match

# Modes

* Siege: push three lanes, take down the towers, crack open the Nexus and finish it with an orbital laser
* Blitz: a quick 5 to 7 minute match with no towers. Capture all 3 zones to open up the Nexus, then destroy it to win
* Training: a course that teaches you every system step by step

# Mechs

* Three weapons you swap on the fly, each with its own element: Pulse Lasers that corrode armor, a Rail Lance that pierces and sets targets on fire, and a Plasma Shotgun whose hits chain lightning
* Fast movement with boosting, dashing, afterburner flight and a perfect dodge that slows time around you
* A thermal sniper rifle your commander drops onto your mech that shoots through walls, homing missiles, a Beam Cannon, and a Shield Bubble
* Four abilities (Shatterfrost, Reactor Surge, Judgement, Orbital Hammer) and even MORE missiles with a Missile Storm ultimate

# Commander

* Deploy and lead the army, capture zones and earn requisition to spend
* Call in tactical abilities like airstrikes and the orbital laser
* Call in a siege tank that drops onto the field, pushes a lane and shells towers. Both mechs can hop on with one button and ride it into battle, firing from the deck

# Enemies

* 14 enemy types so far: 7 kinds of swarm units, 4 elites, and 3 bosses
* The swarm keeps growing the longer the match goes, up to 50,000 enemies on the field at once

# Buffs

* Collect salvage during a match and pick upgrades that power up the whole party
* Common, rare and legendary upgrades that stack and change how you play

# Skill trees

* Earn Marks every match and spend them in skill trees for your mech, your army and your commander
* Each tree has keystones that change your playstyle

# Highlights and replays

* Play of the game and match highlights at the end of every game
* Watch them back or save them as clips
* Full stats and a grade for every player

# Live patch notes

* A What's New panel in the lobby that updates with every release, listing new features, improvements and fixes
* An Up Next line so you can see what's coming before it lands

# Technical details

* Runs in the browser, written in TypeScript with Three.js for rendering and Vite for builds
* The whole simulation runs on its own worker thread with a fixed tick, and every player's game runs the exact same steps, so only player inputs go over the network (peer to peer through PeerJS, with a relay fallback)
* Units are drawn with GPU instancing, which is what lets 50,000+ of them stay on screen without the frame rate falling apart
* Every model is built in Blender from Python scripts and exported as GLB, and most of the animation (walk cycles, recoil, turrets, the boss rigs) is done in code
* Thousands of automated tests check the simulation stays in sync and that fixes don't break old ones

comments.author: challengethegods
comments.body:
as an armored core fan, this looks phenomenal.  
the only thing I thought was a let down in the video was the scale of the mech compared to the tiny enemies crawling around at their feet, just because it makes them seem like inconsequential cannon fodder rather than a huge war going on.  probably it's fine if they are 'smaller' than the mech, but not so small to be stepped on... I suppose in order to have the same visuals of the larger formations the mech itself would be considered too large here rather than the little guys being too small. Trying to make the swarms larger models at this point might be an issue, but anyway, it looks awesome.

replies.author: Reasonable-Reason901
replies.body: Thank you so much for the feedback. Scale is something I’ve been thinking about as well and it’s not really a thing I was ever very intentional with. There’s definitely going to be a sort of ceiling to work around, but I think one possible answer could be just increasing the presence of elites more so there’s both the fodder and more threatening units that actually can wipe your army if left unchecked. Bosses are also going to be a huge factor in the overall balance of things. I’ll definitely do some thinking on this. Thanks again, this is super helpful to hear.
